name: What is the cheapest way to remodel a small bathroom?

mainEntity.name: What is the cheapest way to update a small bathroom without doing a full gut renovation?
mainEntity.text: What is the cheapest way to update a small bathroom without doing a full gut renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lowest-cost bathroom remodel usually starts with preserving the footprint and avoiding plumbing relocation. In a small bath, that means leaving the toilet, sink, and shower where they are, then focusing money on visible upgrades such as the vanity, mirror, lighting, hardware, paint, and new flooring or wall tile only where needed. Re-glazing a tub can be cheaper than replacing it, and a new shower door can change the look without a full rebuild. The biggest cost jumps come from moving wet walls, rebuilding a shower pan, or opening walls to repair hidden damage. If budget is the main concern, prioritize waterproofing, ventilation, and durable finishes before decorative extras. Ask for a bid that separates must-have repairs from cosmetic upgrades so you can phase the project if needed.
acceptedAnswer.description: The cheapest way to remodel a small bathroom is to keep the existing layout and reuse as many plumbing locations as possible. Painting, replacing the vanity, updating the toilet, refinishing the tub, and installing new lighting or mirrors usually cost less than moving walls, drains, or shower plumbing.
